items.title: Delhi court denies bail to lawyer accused in Satya Niketan building collapse
items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday denied bail to Shubham Tyagi, an advocate and one of the accused in the case related to the collapse of a paying-guest (PG) building in Satya Niketan that killed seven people. Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Dhirendra Rana of the Patiala House Courts said Tyagi, who was one of the operators of the PG, had failed to ensure the safety of students staying at the premises despite being aware of ongoing construction work in the building. The court noted that students had complained about the construction work, following which Tyagi and his co-accused Sudhanshu Lovenish Kumar allegedly threatened that they would have to vacate the premises if they continued raising objections. "He could have easily foreseen the danger on account of illegal construction activities but he prioritized his financial benefits above the life and safety of innocent students/labours," the Court said. It said that Tyagi is a lawyer and yet, he did not follow the law. Such accused persons must be dealt with an "iron hand", the Court added.
